text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Rabobank runs into legal problems in U.S. following takeover of the Robeco group. (p1)
- Dutch life-insurers propose Dfl 400 million safety net for troubled life-insurance companies. (p1)
- Dutch PTT (KPN) considers separate listings for postal and telecom arms. (p1)
- South of Netherlands shows more rapid economic growth than north this year. (p1)
- Computer producer Tulip is not to go ahead with an unnamed Asian partner. (p1)
- U.S. chips industry supplier Applied Materials considers damages claim against Dutch counterpart ASMI. (p1)
- Dutch railways NS postpones sale of rail-building unit to 1997. (p3)
- Dutch unit of Germany's electronics giant Siemens says outlook for 1996/1997 fiscal year is good. (p3)
VOLKSKRANT
- Steelmaker Hoogovens not prepared to participate in Belgian steelconcern Boel unless Boel restructured first. (p2)
- Bankruptcies this year will be lower than in 1995, but fall not as big as expected. (p2)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM raises price of flights by between three and five percent today. (p2)
- Supermarkets thrive due to extended opening hours since July 1. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Germany rejects Netherlands' 6.0 billion guilders claim for natural gas. (p1)
- Prisoners allowed to watch porn videos, reveals justice minister. (p1)
- Dutch population will continue to grow to 17.2 million in 2034, according to Central Statistics Bureau (CBS). (p3)
- Majority in parliament wants stock exchange transactions by top executives to be open for inspection. (p25)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Large number of filling stations boycott introduction of chipcard because of high costs. (p10)
TROUW
- France apologises for farmers who assaulted Dutch truckers. (p1)
- Philips Electronics reckons automation unit Origin will quadruple turnover in four years'. (p7)
